milestone: MSCA-DN assessment framework, ticket R04 of plans/pe08_review_and_pe09_handoff_tickets.md: prepare revision-specific fidelity declarations, after R01 (the durable declaration input), R02 (the operator review table) and R03 (the semantic adjudications)
authority: CLAUDE.md §9.1 (docs/ is the durable record), §9.4 (a decision that affects future interpretation is written here), §9.5 (outputs reproducible from documented inputs), §10.5 (every material claim names its tiered source), §12.1 (an output names its inputs, states its inferences and flags its assumptions), §12.2 (the four statuses), §12.4 (a missing mandatory input is a gate failure), §13.3 (no invented project fact), §15 (explicit failure over fabricated completion); spec decision 9 (the register's two halves and the two independent fields per sub-section) and decision 18 (the provenance header).

problem.basis: read in the two committed registers and in the dispositions record at 1eddc81
problem.statement: Both declared halves are empty, so every ESR disposition that leans on evidence preservation leans on a document-wide provenance declaration instead of a per-sub-section one.
detail: declared.sub_sections is an empty list in both docs/tier3_project_instantiation/source_materials/msca_dn/fidelity_register.json and docs/tier3_project_instantiation/source_materials/msca_dn/fidelity_register_resolved_fixes.json.
The dispositions record states evidence_preserved_status 'Assumed' throughout and gives the reason: the declared half is unfilled, so the derived half and the provenance declarations are the basis.
Every evidence_basis pointer in that record points at provenance/transformation/* or derived/*. None points at a declared row, because there is none.
Three rows of the active review notes carry recommendation 'revisit_after_declaration', and six more carry 'revisit_after_private_network'.

decision.basis: the implementation in tools/draft_fidelity_declarations.py, the artifacts it wrote, and the verification below
decision.what_was_produced: One draft record per revision under docs/tier4_orchestration_state/msca_dn/declarations/ (draft_sanitised_v1.json, draft_resolved_fixes.json), each covering that revision's 15-sub-section derived inventory exactly once, plus one Markdown review checklist across both (review_checklist.md). No declaration input was written, and neither register was changed.
decision.drafts_live_in_tier_4_not_tier_3: A draft is a proposal for operator review, so it is a Tier 4 review artifact. The adoptable payload sits inside the draft under 'declaration_input', byte-for-byte what the operator's input would hold, and 'py -3.10 -m tools.draft_fidelity_declarations --emit-input <revision>' prints it to stdout. The renderer has no code path that writes into docs/tier3_project_instantiation/source_materials/msca_dn/declarations/, and a test asserts that directory still holds only its README.
decision.deterministic_and_claude_free: The renderer reads committed artifacts only — the two registers, the two import manifests, the dispositions record and the active review notes — and transforms them. It measures nothing itself, invokes no Claude and evaluates no gate, so --check is a byte-equal replay and the drafts are reproducible from their documented inputs (§9.5).

the_three_claims.rule: Ticket R04 step 3 requires three claims to stay separate, because each is checkable in a different place. Every drafted row names which claim each of its fields speaks to, under 'claim_scope'.
the_three_claims.extraction_fidelity_against_the_sanitise: The row's 'presence' field. Confirmed, from the derived half's own counts for that sub-section — prose blocks, table rows, characters, extracted claims, derived and declared page ranges — and the file-level character accounting. Its 'scope_limit' says in the artifact that this is not a statement about the original.
the_three_claims.difference_between_the_sanitised_revisio: The row's 'revision_difference' field. Confirmed, from the import manifest's page-by-page comparison and the two derived halves. Only sub-section 3.1 differs between the revisions: page 45 was re-typeset, paragraphs 145 to 142, characters 27977 to 28087. The first revision's rows record that it has no predecessor, and name the successor's one changed page.
the_three_claims.fidelity_against_the_submitted_original: The row's 'fidelity_to_submitted_original' field. Unresolved for every sub-section of both revisions, with the basis naming provenance/authoritative_original and the resolution naming PE-09. No measurement available here can raise it.
the_three_claims.where_transformation_sits: The register's 'transformation' field sits on the third claim, one step above the per-sub-section judgment: it carries the operator's PE-01 declaration about the document as a whole. Its status is Assumed, the weaker of the two it spans, and its basis names the parts that measurement does confirm document-wide — zero images on any page, all four citation-marker counts zero, the body point size, and the sub-section's own rendered table-row count. Its 'not_measured' field states what has no measurement anywhere: how much prose moved in that sub-section, and whether any passage was removed rather than rewritten.

decision.no_format_change_was_needed: R04 step 5 permits the smallest justified format change if the format cannot carry a necessary uncertainty. None was needed. tools/fidelity_declarations.py requires a sub_section_id in the revision's inventory and a non-empty presence and transformation, and carries every further field through untouched. The two extra claim fields, the title, the claim_scope tags and the per-row attribution therefore travel as ordinary extra fields. No enum was coined: every status is one of CLAUDE.md §12.2's four, and review_state reuses the single value the R02 review notes already use.
decision.measured_facts_do_not_become_fidelity_cl: Step 4. Presence is Confirmed and bounded in the artifact by its own scope_limit. Zero extraction loss is recorded as a file-level accounting fact inside the presence basis, never as preservation. A test asserts presence and transformation differ in value, basis, claim scope and status on every row of both revisions.
decision.extraction_caveats_qualify_presence_only: Each presence field carries the caveats the manifest records inside that sub-section: the page-map discrepancy for sub-section 8, the three table cells whose characters are present but not in page reading order for 3.1, and the one claim without a span for 3.2. A spanless claim is attributed by its claim id, which the importer forms as '<sub_section_id>-cNNN', not by page range: 3.1 ends on page 65 and 3.2 begins there, so a page rule would put 3.2's claim on both.
decision.prior_operator_declarations: Step 6. The operator's declarations are read from the durable input, not from the register. R01 settled that ownership: the register's declared half is a rendering of the input, so a register rendered before the last edit to the input is stale rather than a source. A row the input declares is carried into the payload byte-for-byte and never redrafted, restated or raised to a stronger status; the draft fills only the sub-sections the input does not declare, and prior_declarations records which rows are which. A row only the register holds is reported under declared_only_in_the_register with a note, not adopted: it is either a withdrawal or a row typed into the output, and tools/fidelity_declarations.guard_against_silent_loss is what tells the two apart. Both inputs are absent today, so all 30 rows are drafted. A prior row naming a sub-section outside the derived inventory is a refusal.
decision.no_row_impersonates_the_operator: Every drafted row carries declared_by 'R04 draft, pending operator confirmation; replace with the operator's own attribution on adoption' and review_state 'agent_drafted_pending_operator_review'. The draft record type is 'fidelity_declaration_draft', distinct from the input's 'fidelity_declarations', so a draft cannot be mistaken for the input it proposes. There is no 'approved' value anywhere in the renderer.

the_contradicted_declaration.statement: Step 7. The provenance header declares reformatting.body_point_size as 12 in both revisions. In the revised revision that declaration is contradicted by measurement; in the first one it holds.
the_contradicted_declaration.evidence: derived/body_point_size of the revised register: the body is 12.0 pt over 117600 characters, 1040 characters sit at 10.0 pt and are bullets and spaces only, and 458 characters sit at 9.8 pt over a character set carrying letters and digits — so other_sizes_are_bullets_and_spaces_only is false. The same register's provenance/known_extraction_limitations/prose_below_the_body_point_size records the same figure. In the first revision the only other size is the 10.0 pt bullets, and the flag is true.
the_contradicted_declaration.proposal: Replace the bare 12 with a statement that the body of the revised revision is set at 12.0 pt except for 458 characters at 9.8 pt that carry prose rather than bullets, naming derived/body_point_size as the measurement.
the_contradicted_declaration.status: The contradiction itself is Confirmed. Which page carries the smaller prose is Inferred and is deliberately not asserted: the only changed page of this revision is the one the manifest names, and the derived half records no page for the size.
the_contradicted_declaration.not_applied: The declaration is the operator's. Applying the correction would edit the provenance literal in tools/author_msca_dn_workspace.py and change the register's bytes, so it is recorded as a proposal with reviewer status 'agent_drafted_pending_operator_review'. A test asserts the register still declares 12.

decision.declarations_that_hold_or_are_already_qu: The same pass checks three more provenance declarations per revision so the check is visible rather than absent. transformation/figures holds (zero images on any page) and transformation/citations holds (all four marker counts zero). reformatting/table_3_1a is 'qualified_in_place': the measured label-block counts differ from a uniform reading, and the derived half's own basis already says they are recorded as measured and may differ, so no correction is proposed.

esr_dependencies.rule: Step 8. A disposition is attached to a sub-section only where the dispositions record names one — in a current_evidence reference, or in an evidence_basis pointer into derived/sub_sections/. Nothing is inferred from wording.
esr_dependencies.result: Eleven sub-sections of the revised revision carry at least one dependent observation, each with its disposition, the active review notes' recommendation, and what a confirmed declaration would change. That last field is a statement about how the disposition vocabulary works, written per disposition value, not a new finding.
esr_dependencies.unattached: ESR-I-S01 is recommended for revisiting after a declaration and the dispositions record names no sub-section for it. It is listed separately with the operator question 'name the sub-section whose declaration this row depends on', rather than assigned to a guess. The appendix secondment table its note concerns cannot be located from the recorded pointers, and a text search over the candidate finds 'secondment' in eleven sub-sections, so no attribution is supportable.
esr_dependencies.the_first_revision_has_none: No ESR disposition binds sanitised_v1: the comparison is bound to the revised register. That draft records the fact and an empty dependency list, rather than borrowing the revised revision's.

decision.active_review_notes_resolution: The notes record that no other notes record supersedes. R03's record names R02's under 'supersedes', so the R03 reading is the current one. Two unsuperseded records would be a refusal rather than a silent pick.

hash_dependencies.rule: Acceptance 6. Measured, not listed by hand: docs/, workspaces/ and plans/ are scanned for each register's full sha256 and for its first 16 characters, which is the prefix the review reports print.
hash_dependencies.sanitised_v1: Pinned by the PE-03 decision log record and the PE-03 validation report, both by full sha256.
hash_dependencies.resolved_fixes: Pinned by comparison_f60ae6e0a2a1_0001.json and semantic_adjudications_f60ae6e0a2a1.json by full sha256, and by operator_review_9732dde50039_0001.md and _0002.md by prefix.
hash_dependencies.self_reference_excluded: The drafts' own directory is excluded from the scan. A draft records the register hash itself, so including it would make the scan a fixed point of its own output.
hash_dependencies.the_import_manifest: Enumerated too, and unaffected. The manifest renders the derived half and the page comparison, neither of which reads a declaration, so adoption leaves its bytes as they are. The same scan over each manifest's hash finds no artifact pinning it, and the block records that measurement rather than the assertion.
hash_dependencies.preservation: A re-recording after adoption is a successor artifact, never an edit in place: a comparison that pinned the old hash stays replayable from the register version it names.

decision.adoption_is_the_operators_act: Each draft carries an adoption block: the target path, the seven steps, the register sha256 before adoption, the artifacts that pin it, and the artifacts that name it by path. Step 2 of that list is replacing every row's declared_by. No adoption or provenance record is written here, because no operator review has been recorded; the checklist states what such a record must carry.

verification.basis: run on 2026-10-07 in the working tree of this branch
verification.new_tests: tests/test_msca_dn_declaration_drafts.py, 73 tests. The payload loads through tools.fidelity_declarations on a temporary root and resolves against the inventory the committed register lists; a draft is not a declaration record. Inventory coverage: every sub-section once, in inventory order, for both revisions, and the two drafts are distinct records. Claims and statuses: presence and transformation differ in value, basis, claim scope and status on every row; every field names a declared claim scope; every status is one of the four; original fidelity is Unresolved everywhere with a basis naming the private network and a stated resolution; presence carries its scope limit; transformation is Assumed while each measured part is Confirmed; no row claims operator authorship. Measured facts: every number in a presence basis is the register's own derived row, including both page ranges and the file-level accounting; the set of sub-sections the draft calls changed equals the set the two registers actually differ on; the first revision declares no predecessor; a spanless claim lands on the sub-section its id names and on no other. Declaration checks: every check names a register pointer and one of three verdicts; the uniform body size is contradicted exactly where other_sizes_are_bullets_and_spaces_only is false; the contradicted row carries a proposal, a status, a basis and a reviewer status, and the register still declares 12. ESR dependencies: only the bound revision carries them; every declaration-dependent row of the active notes is either attached or listed with a question, and the two sets are disjoint; an unattached row asks rather than guesses; every attached row's disposition matches the dispositions record; the active notes are the unsuperseded ones. Prior declarations: a prior row wins unchanged over the draft, a prior row outside the inventory is refused, both registers declare nothing today, a declaration written to the input is carried through and the input is then listed among the draft's own inputs, and a row only the register holds is reported with a note rather than adopted. Hash dependencies: every pinned artifact really records the hash or its prefix, every path reference really names the register, the two replay-critical artifacts of the revised revision are listed, the import manifest is enumerated with no hash dependents and changed_by_adoption false, and the drafts' own directory is excluded. Determinism: the committed artifacts are reproducible (check() is empty), two renderings agree byte for byte, check() writes nothing, the checklist covers both revisions and every sub-section of each, --emit-input prints the payload and writes nothing, and an unknown revision is refused. Adoption: with the declaration directory pointed outside the repository, each register re-renders holding every drafted row unchanged and records the input's sha256; adoption changes the register bytes while the committed file stays as it is; neither revision reads the other's declarations; and the production declaration directory still holds only its README.

consequences.nothing_is_declared_yet: Both registers still carry an empty declared half, every disposition still rests on the document-wide provenance declaration, and no recorded hash changed. R04 prepares; it does not adopt.
consequences.what_adoption_will_cost: Adopting either payload rewrites that register, so the artifacts each draft lists under adoption/pinned_by_hash must be re-recorded as successors or explained. The R01 record already warned of this; R04 enumerates it per revision.
consequences.what_r05_can_do_with_this: Once a declaration is adopted, a successor dispositions record can point evidence_basis at declared/sub_sections/<id> instead of provenance/transformation, and the three 'revisit_after_declaration' rows gain a per-sub-section basis. Until then R05 must keep evidence_preserved_status at Assumed.
consequences.what_stays_for_pe_09: Every fidelity_to_submitted_original row, all 30 of them, and the six observations the active notes recommend revisiting after the private network. Nothing available here can resolve them.
consequences.a_new_artifact_naming_a_register_makes_t: The adoption block is measured by scanning docs/, workspaces/ and plans/, so a later committed artifact that names a register or its hash fails 'py -3.10 -m tools.draft_fidelity_declarations --check' until the drafts are re-rendered. This happened once while writing this record: naming both registers here added two rows to referenced_by_path. The coupling is intended — an enumeration that went out of date silently would be worse than one that fails a check.
consequences.new_tier_4_files: Four, counting this record. The two closed-demo tests that recount the Tier 3/4/5 file tree (test_demo_candidate_blind_baseline.py leakage scan and test_demo_report.py scan count) were already failing on this branch and now differ by that many more files.
